results.note: Matches 2.1 Procedure (PDF p. 3) and the p. 3 part of Introduction paragraph 3. 'Participating federal, state, local and tribal agencies' joins two adjacent sentences fairly.
All counts, β/SE/p and percentages checked on rendered pp. 1-3, 6 and recomputed; 68/492 and 635/2,174 correct. My Fig. 1 pixel readings show the share equals pill/(pill+powder) in every quarter.

My 300-dpi pixel readings: powder peak about 2,058 (2021 Q3; 'about 2,060' fits better), pill seizures about 675 (Q3), pills about 2.73 million and powder about 2,919 kg (Q2); shares 0.215, 0.173; 0.292 highest.
Discussion paragraph 4 (p. 4) and 4.1 Limitations (pp. 5-6) match. The authors then call it 'more than plausible' that seizures reflect greater overall availability; not needed here.

key_findings.note: My readings (300 dpi, pixel measurement): powder-seizure peak about 2,058 (about 2,060 rather than 2,050); pills seized about 1.77 million (2020 Q3) and about 0.89 million (2020 Q4); fitted share at 2021 Q4 about 0.27. All within reading error.
The authors also cite rising illicit production, perceived abundance and ease of transport (DEA), and hedge the conclusion as 'more than plausible'.

reporting_issues.note: My trace of the Fig. 2 right fitted curve: quarter-to-quarter rises grow from about 0.11 to about 0.25 million, then shrink to about 0.21 million, so it is clearly curved.
My readings at 2018 Q1: fitted line about -0.10 million, band lower edge about -0.59 million; powder-weight band about -43 kg; pill-seizure band about -13.
Fig. 1 caption and axis also say 'out of all fentanyl seizures' / 'of Total Seizures'; my quarterly readings fit pill/(pill+powder) in all 16 quarters.

risk_of_bias.note: Design (registry), JBI prevalence checklist and overall moderate (high as a supply indicator) agreed.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor: the counterfeit-pill risk conclusion rests on cited literature, as the card says.

missed: Discussion paragraph 3 (PDF p. 4) says the results corroborate a study finding no COVID-19 dip and that fentanyl availability 'increased consistently', but Figs 1-2 show quarterly falls (powder seizures about 1,071 to 950, 2020 Q1-Q2, and about 1,436 to 1,224, 2020 Q3-Q4; pills seized about 1.77 to 0.89 million, 2020 Q3-Q4): stated more strongly than the quarterly data.
